stem:
A Geiger–Müller (G–M) tube is a device that can detect beta-radiation. A student places paper between a radioactive source emitting beta-radiation and a G–M tube, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The G–M tube is connected to a rate-meter which records the count rate *R*.

The thickness *t* of the paper is measured in two different places using a micrometer.

The student repeats the experiment for different thicknesses of paper.

It is suggested that *R* and *t* are related by the equation

$R = R_0 e^{-bc9t}$

where *R*₀ is the count rate without any paper and *μ* is a constant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of ln *R* on the *y*-axis against *t* on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The two measurements of thickness are *t*₁ and *t*₂. Values of *t*₁, *t*₂ and *R* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of average *t* / mm and ln (*R* / s⁻¹) in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in average *t*.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of ln (*R* / s⁻¹) against average *t* / mm. Include error bars for average *t*.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Both lines should be clearly labelled.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *μ* and *R*₀. Include the absolute uncertainties in your values and include appropriate units.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The experiment is repeated using a different thickness of paper.

Determine the value of *t* that would give a value of *R* of 20.0 s⁻¹.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A radioactive source and a G–M tube are positioned on a bench with a sheet of paper between them, and the tube is connected to a rate-meter.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for t₁ / mm, t₂ / mm, average t / mm, R / s⁻¹ and ln (R / s⁻¹), with six rows of t₁, t₂ and R values and blank average-thickness and logarithm cells.
A blank graph grid with ln (R / s⁻¹) on the vertical axis from 3.35 to 3.90 and t / mm on the horizontal axis from 0.1 to 0.8.

notes: The exponent in the equation was unclear in the text rendering.
problems: part d: numeric part needs answer {symbol, unit} (either may be null)
